$comment: Converted by desmap2proto from sim/desmap/tests/fixtures/cencora_phase1.json. The old file places everything on one 154 x 103 integer grid of 1000 mm cells; here the same site is millimetre-first. Legacy identifiers ride as external_ids, never as identity. Every value the old format could not state is a converter parameter and is listed in this fixture's ledger under tools/desmap2proto/ledgers/.

doc.name: cencora_phase1.json world (converted from a desmap v3 fixture)

frame.$comment: The old fixture's grid: 154 wide x 103 deep, cell_size_mm 1000. An old index names a cell, and a cell's place is its centre, so index [c,r] reads as millimetres [1000c+500, 1000r+500]: the pitch as the scale, half a cell as the translation. Declared for projection only — nothing below is positioned in it. The scale is positive: desmap fixtures are self-consistent, unlike the Map Creator exports that need a mirror, and the half-cell offset is positive with it.

tiling.$comment: The old format's implicit everywhere-grid, made explicit: 154 x 103 cells at the grid's own 1000 mm pitch. No flow is declared, so it compiles two_way (SPEC §5: flow restricts, never permits), which is what the old grid meant.

template.$comment: One bay, presenting its boards on the `+y` face. That face is on the steel because it is a fact about the steel; which face the STORAGE is worked from, and by whom, is the access declared beside each run. The old `sides` enum said both at once and named one.

rack.$comment: One bay of the old zone: each grid row of a relay zone is one rack position holding vertical_tote_capacity = 10 storage levels and one handoff board, written as one list of level heights bottom-up. The shelf count is the source's; the bay's length, depth, shelf spacing, board height, board position and the reach of its relay level are not in the old format at all and are converter parameters (see the fixture's ledger). The face the board presents on is the old `sides` enum read back out.
